Subject: POC environment roadmap & owners — Lumina Health

Hi Ava / Thomas —

Thanks again for the call today — good discussion and clear priorities. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we have alignment before we lock dates.

Goal of the 4-week POC: validate end-to-end clinical note generation and QA gating with your anonymized sample data, and measure latency/throughput at representative session sizes. Success criteria (proposed):
- Precision: model output pass rate >= 92% on the provided QA prompt set (30 prompts)
- Latency: 95th percentile inference latency <= 450ms for single-turn flows
- Cost throughput: token cost per 1k tokens aligns with Redwood Optimize baseline for the chosen model (we'll provide a forecast)
- Integration: automated upload + retrieval from your S3 bucket and a working webhook to your review UI

Environment options we discussed (pros/cons):
1) Hosted Sandbox (fastest onboarding) — Redwood-hosted, quickest to start (48–72h), limited to synthetic data for initial eval unless you allow sample uploads. Good to get results fast for model validation.
2) Dedicated Sandbox (reserved GPUs for you) — predictable throughput, better for high-concurrency tests, ~1 week to provision depending on capacity.
3) VPC Trial (preferred for PHI/SSO) — private networking and KMS integration, requires network peering and SSO config; estimate 2–3 weeks to stand up for first region.

Recommended path (to balance speed + security): start Hosted Sandbox immediately for a 1–2 week rapid model validation and parallel-track VPC setup so we can flip to private routing for final evaluation. That reduces time-to-insight while meeting your security gating.

Proposed owners / asks:
- Lumina: confirm sample data payload size & S3 transfer details, and provide SSO metadata (if you want SAML for the console). (Action: Ava)
- Redwood AE (Ben): finalize MAP and pricing estimate for Dedicated vs Hosted run rates. (Action: Ben)
- Redwood SE (Karthik): scope VPC peering requirements and list of IPs/CIDRs + infra checklist. (Action: Karthik)
- Redwood (Jasmine): coordinate timeline and M.A.P., schedule kick-off once owners confirm. (Action: Jasmine)

Attachments: I attached a first-pass Mutual Action Plan template and our SOC2 questionnaire we discussed — fill what you can and we’ll iterate.

Next proposed step: if you agree, we’ll schedule a 30-min kick-off on Monday to agree timelines and get Hosted Sandbox credentials out the same day. Please confirm preferred kick-off window (Mon/Tues morning PT).

Thanks —
Jasmine Liu

Thanks Jasmine — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- Security: our default requirement is that any PHI or production-like clinical notes must be within a VPC with KMS key control and SAML access for reviewers. We can start with de-identified data in a hosted sandbox for early model checks, but the main goal is a VPC-backed run for any realistic evaluation.
- Timing: can your team realistically have a VPC trial ready for a small pilot in 2–3 weeks? Our security lead (cc’d: Thomas) needs to understand the network/peering timeline.
- Cost: please include a rough delta between Hosted Sandbox and Dedicated Sandbox (monthly burn estimate) in the MAP so execs can greenlight budget.

We’ll start filling the MAP this weekend — sending our SSO metadata and an anonymized sample payload separately.

Ava

Hi Ava / Thomas —

Appreciate the call and the constraints you’ve shared. Quick financial framing so you have something for your execs:
- Hosted Sandbox (temporary): $0 initial for 14-day eval (we absorb infra), estimated incremental token cost only — ideal for the rapid model pass/fail.
- Dedicated Sandbox (reserved GPUs): roughly $6k-$9k/month for a small reserved pool that matches the concurrency you described (2–4 concurrent workers) — I’ll include ranges in the MAP.
- VPC Trial: one-time setup fee depending on peering complexity (~$2k–$5k) + dedicated bandwidth cost if you need sustained throughput; ongoing compute looks similar to Dedicated.

Operational proposal (to enable both speed + security):
1) Provision Hosted Sandbox immediately and run the 1-week model validation using your de-identified payload (starts within 48–72h of sign-off).
2) Parallel ticket to Redwood Infra for VPC peering and KMS setup (we’ll need your security/infra contact and a point of contact — Thomas?)
3) By week 2–3, migrate evaluation traffic to the VPC trial for final gating.

I’ll push a draft MAP into the HubSpot deal and attach a pricing appendix. Jasmine — can you schedule the kick-off and confirm Mon 25 May 9:00–10:30 PT?

Thanks,

Hi all —

Technical notes from the SE lens (to help your security team evaluate):
- VPC setup: we require one outbound peering connection from your VPC to our managed egress with a small set of CIDRs. Typical steps: exchange SAs, schedule a peering window, validate routes and firewall rules, and test with a small traffic generator. See our runbook: https://redwood.app/runbooks/vpc-onboarding
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS) — we’ll request a grant for the Redwood service principal.
- Data flow for the POC: S3 -> preprocessor (Lumina) -> Redwood inference (VPC) -> review webhook (Lumina). If you need offline review we can write outputs to a locked S3 bucket you control.
- Model choices: for clinical notes we recommend Redwood-clinical-1 (optimized tokens/latency) or open-llm-9b-quant for lower cost tests. I’ll bring latency/cost estimates into the MAP appendix.

Required info from Lumina to scope the VPC:
- CIDRs/IPs for peering and any firewall egress rules
- SAML metadata for SSO if you want console access bound to your IdP
- A sample anonymized payload (30–50 notes) and representative token counts

Timeline (rough):
- Hosted sandbox credentialing: 48–72h after sign-off
- VPC peering + KMS grants: 10–18 business days (depending on ticket queue and your infra availability)

If you want, I’ll spin up a short checklist doc and a small Terraform snippet we can share with your infra folks.

Thanks —
